page: Google Cloud Platform n2d-highmem-32 is a memory-dense virtual machine configuration powered by third-generation AMD EPYC 7B13 processors built on the x86_64 architecture. The instance provisions 32 virtual CPUs derived from 16 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading across dedicated allocations. Compute resources are coupled with 256 GB of system memory, yielding an 8 GB per vCPU ratio. Local storage is not bundled, requiring persistent network-attached storage volumes for stateful operations, and dedicated hardware acceleration is absent with zero GPUs configured.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong single-core compute performance alongside elevated memory throughput, highlighted by a top-quartile PassMark memory score and top-quartile stress-ng single-core rating. Multi-threaded evaluations, including Geekbench multi-core (13,199) and PassMark CPU (39,043.35), place the instance squarely within average comparative distributions. Memory bandwidth reaches 114.25 GB/sec for large un-cached reads and 62.9 GB/sec for writes, sustaining high operational frequency across intensive tasks such as Redis operations, which registered 31.25 million SET operations per second.

From a cost-efficiency and architectural standpoint, the instance balances high RAM density against mid-range parallel processing capabilities without incurring GPU overhead. While competitive for compute tasks requiring significant memory headroom, workloads involving large-parameter LLM inference face execution constraints, as evidenced by bottom-quartile throughput on 70B model prompt processing. As a result, this server type is best suited for in-memory databases, memory-bound caching layers, large enterprise analytics, and medium-scale compilation or data transformation pipelines.
description: Google Cloud Platform n2d-highmem-32 is a memory-oriented virtual instance powered by AMD EPYC 7B13 processors on the x86_64 architecture. It provides 32 vCPUs from 16 dedicated physical cores paired with 256 GB of RAM, offering an elevated 8 GB per vCPU ratio. The configuration excludes local disk storage and discrete GPUs, relying on networked block storage for persistent data. Performance profiles highlight strong single-core CPU execution and top-quartile PassMark memory metrics, while overall multi-threaded throughput and memory bandwidth fall within average industry benchmarks. With high memory density relative to compute resources, the instance delivers solid efficiency for workloads requiring substantial capacity without the cost profile of GPU acceleration. The n2d-highmem-32 is well aligned with memory-intensive workloads including in-memory caching systems such as Redis, relational and non-relational database management systems, data processing pipelines, and software compilation tasks.
